message.content:
Aristotelian scholars and Ptolemaic astronomers such as Johannes Stöffler criticized Nicolaus Copernicus for rejecting a fixed Earth.  
The Jesuit Christoph Clavius and the astronomer Tycho Brahe later challenged the full Copernican system.  
Theologian Martin Luther also condemned the model in remarks that argued it contradicted Scripture.  
Did these critics include university philosophers, Jesuit astronomers, and religious commentators?  
Which specific opponents raised objections from physics, parallax, and Scripture?  
How did Copernican astronomy survive such early and later resistance?  
What a controversy the motion of the Earth created!  
How many learned critics defended the ancient geocentric view!  
So strong was the resistance to Copernicus!
